summary.en: Choose headers and use conversion, sorting, searching, pseudo-random, process and time facilities with explicit contracts.
summary.bn: হেডার বেছে conversion, sorting, searching, pseudo-random সংখ্যা ও সময়ের ফাংশন সঠিকভাবে ব্যবহার করো।

sections.title: Reuse a tool after reading its label
Headers tell the compiler which interface you mean
Inspect useful library contracts in small programs
Ask whether you need a date or CPU work
Keep hidden assumptions out of utility calls
A C17 tour with long-established interfaces
Choose the operation and check its contract

examples.title: Sort roll numbers before binary searching the same ordering
examples.explanationHtml: qsort rearranges the array into ascending order. bsearch then uses the same comparator and element size. The comparator compares rather than subtracting, avoiding overflow for extreme signed values.

examples.title: Compare convenient conversion with complete validation
examples.explanationHtml: Both calls obtain the representable prefix 72, but strtol also exposes the remaining x. atoi offers no equivalent end-pointer or suitable range-error interface. Neither call makes the complete string a valid mark by itself.

examples.title: Demonstrate seeded repeatability without assuming a rand sequence
examples.explanationHtml: Reseeding with the same seed repeats the sequence within the implementation. The numeric sequence itself is not portable, so the program prints only guaranteed comparisons. rand is not suitable for passwords or other security decisions.

examples.title: Format a constructed calendar and measure a known interval
examples.explanationHtml: struct tm stores years since 1900 and months from zero. The constructed date avoids a changing wall-clock result. Equal time_t values have a zero difference; the program does not assume a portable epoch representation or call abs on INT_MIN.

practice.title: Sort a bounded mark list and select its middle element
practice.statementHtml: Read an odd n from 1 through 9, then n marks from 0 through 100. Sort with qsort and print the median at index n/2. Input tokens fit int; invalid count, missing marks or invalid marks print invalid.
hints: Require odd length before indexing the median.

practice.title: Find a requested roll with bsearch
practice.statementHtml: Read one integer key from -1000 through 1000. Search the already sorted array {101, 103, 107, 109}. Print found or missing. Print invalid when no integer is read.
hints: Pass a pointer to the key.
Keep count and element width distinct.

practice.title: Choose a source of time for two different questions
practice.statementHtml: Explain the difference between recording a calendar instant and measuring CPU time. State failure checks and why raw time_t subtraction is not the portable calendar difference operation.
practice.answerHtml: time returns a calendar-time representation and indicates unavailability with (time_t)-1. difftime computes the difference in seconds between two calendar times. clock reports processor-time ticks and can return (clock_t)-1; divide a valid tick difference by CLOCKS_PER_SEC for CPU seconds. CPU time is not wall elapsed time. Do not assume that time_t is a Unix integer epoch on every C implementation.

practice.title: Explain duplicate-key search and stable sorting limits
practice.statementHtml: An array contains several equal keys. What may bsearch return, and does qsort preserve the order of equal elements?
hints: The function names do not promise stable selection.
practice.answerHtml: bsearch may return a matching element without specifying which duplicate is selected. qsort does not promise a stable order for equal elements. If an application requires an earliest match or preserved tie order, add a tie-break key or use an algorithm with that stated guarantee. Keep the comparator consistent with the array ordering used for searching.

quiz.prompt: Which header declares qsort and bsearch?
quiz.explanation: General utility declarations belong to stdlib.h.

quiz.prompt: Why is a - b a risky int comparator?
options: Pointers cannot be compared by value
quiz.explanation: Comparisons combined as (a > b) - (a < b) give the required sign safely.

quiz.prompt: What must hold before bsearch uses an ascending comparator?
options: The array has exactly ten elements
The array is sorted under that comparator
quiz.explanation: Searching assumes the ordering used by its comparison function.

quiz.prompt: What does srand with the same seed promise within one implementation?
options: The same sequence on every C library
Modulo is undefined for unsigned numbers
RAND_MAX + 1 may not be divisible by six
quiz.explanation: Some residues can have more source values than others.

quiz.prompt: Which abs input is unsafe when its positive result cannot fit int?
quiz.explanation: The absolute value must be representable in the return type.

options: Successful return from a helper only
quiz.explanation: exit ends the program; it is not an ordinary helper return.

quiz.prompt: Which field represents November in struct tm?
quiz.explanation: Months count from zero; years count from 1900.

quiz.prompt: Which sign does the overflow-safe comparator produce for 4 and 9?
quiz.explanation: Only a < b is true, so the difference is minus one.

quiz.prompt: How many characters of 18ms are accepted as decimal digits?
quiz.explanation: The prefix has two digits and end points at m.

quiz.prompt: What calendar year does the constructed tm_year represent?

keyPoints.en: Include the header that declares each library interface.
keyPoints.bn: যে লাইব্রেরি ফাংশন ব্যবহার করবে, তার declaration-এর হেডার include করো।

keyPoints.en: Use strtol when complete numeric validation matters.
keyPoints.bn: সংখ্যার পুরো ইনপুট যাচাই করতে strtol ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: qsort and bsearch must agree on element size and ordering.
keyPoints.bn: qsort ও bsearch-এ element-এর আকার ও ordering এক রাখো।

keyPoints.en: Seeded rand is repeatable within an implementation, not secure randomness.
keyPoints.bn: Seed দিলে একই implementation-এ rand-এর ধারা মেলে; এটি নিরাপদ randomness নয়।

keyPoints.en: Use difftime for calendar differences and respect failure sentinels.
keyPoints.bn: Calendar সময়ের পার্থক্যে difftime নাও এবং failure sentinel যাচাই করো।

keyPoints.en: abs requires its positive result to fit the return type.
keyPoints.bn: abs-এর ফলও return type-এ ধরতে হবে; শুধু ইনপুট ধরলেই হয় না।

examQuestions.question: Describe the qsort comparator contract and repair return a - b.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The comparator returns a negative, zero or positive value according to the chosen consistent ordering. It receives pointers to elements. Dereference using the actual element type and return the difference of the two relational results for ascending int order. Subtraction can overflow for distant signed values. qsort need not be stable.

examQuestions.question: Explain why a fixed srand seed is useful for a demonstration but not a portable printed sequence.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The same seed repeats the generator sequence within an implementation, making local experiments repeatable. Different C libraries may implement different generators. Print implementation-independent properties when teaching portability, or explicitly scope a numeric sequence to the documented implementation. rand is unsuitable for security-sensitive values.

examQuestions.question: Compare time, difftime, localtime and strftime.
examQuestions.answerHtml: time obtains a calendar-time value when available. difftime computes a seconds difference without assuming a representation. localtime converts a calendar value into local broken-down fields and may return null. strftime formats those fields into a bounded buffer and returns zero when the requested result does not fit. Check each relevant failure result before using the next stage.
